question.problem:
Find the radius of curvature for the curve $r(t)$ at the point $r(0)$ if the curve and the derivative ${T}^{′}(t)$ of the corresponding unit tangent vector are given by

$$
r(t)=⟨2{e}^{t},\,{e}^{2t},\,t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=\frac{2}{(2{e}^{2t}+1)^{2}}⟨{e}^{2t}-2{e}^{3t},\,2{e}^{2t},\,-2{e}^{2t}⟩\,.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the curve $r(t)$ and the derivative ${T}^{′}(t)$ of the unit tangent, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{t},\,2{e}^{2t},\,1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨2{e}^{0},\,2{e}^{0},\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{9}=3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${T}^{′}(0)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(0) & =\frac{2}{(2{e}^{0}+1)^{2}}⟨{e}^{0}-2{e}^{0},\,2{e}^{0},\,-2{e}^{0}⟩ \\  & =\frac{2}{9}⟨-1,\,2,\,-2⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{9}=\frac{2\cdot 3}{9}=\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $r(0)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{3}{(\frac{2}{3})}=\frac{3\cdot 3}{2}=\frac{9}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
